title: Filtered presentations of small diagrams
statement: Use universes, coherent functor categories, nerves, colimits, accessibility and compactness from [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category] and [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $\lambda<\kappa$ be infinite regular cardinals in the smaller universe, with $\kappa$ uncountable and $\mu^\nu<\kappa$ whenever $\mu<\kappa$ and $\nu<\lambda$. Let $\mathcal C$ be both $\lambda$-accessible and $\kappa$-accessible and let $K$ be a $\kappa$-small simplicial set. Then $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)$ is $\kappa$-accessible. Every diagram $p:K\to\mathcal C$ is a colimit in this functor category of a diagram $q:N(A)\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)$ indexed by a small $\kappa$-filtered partially ordered set $A$, with $q(a)(v)$ $\kappa$-compact for every $a\in A$ and every vertex $v$ of $K$. Each diagram whose values are $\kappa$-compact is $\kappa$-compact as an object of $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)$.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 5.4.4.3, printed p. 434, with its two cardinals denoted here by λ and κ; Proposition 5.3.4.13 for compactness, and Proposition 5.3.1.18 for replacement of a filtered index by a filtered poset. These are exactly the presentations used in Lemma 5.5.4.14, printed pp. 481-482.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal F=\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)$, a quasicategory by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. By [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits], every small $\kappa$-filtered diagram in $\mathcal F$ has a colimit computed at each vertex: the needed colimits exist in $\mathcal C$ by $\kappa$-accessibility [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category]. Restriction to every simplicial subset of K preserves these colimits. The local-smallness clause of [lem-coef-functor-spine-tower-mapping-descent] shows that $\mathcal F$ is locally small.

source.place: Proposition 5.1.2.2; beginning of the proof of Proposition 5.4.4.3 (online, not archived)

proof.text: We prove pointwise $\kappa$-compactness implies compactness of a diagram, retaining an arbitrary small $\kappa$-filtered index I. For an arrow $a:c_0\to c_1$, [lem-coef-infinity-arrow-morphism-square] expresses $\operatorname{Map}(a,b)$ as the homotopy pullback of $\operatorname{Map}(c_0,b_0)$ and $\operatorname{Map}(c_1,b_1)$ over $\operatorname{Map}(c_0,b_1)$. If both $c_i$ are $\kappa$-compact, each of these three functors preserves I-colimits. The finite-limit case of [lem-coef-spaces-kappa-limit-filtered-colimit] makes the pullback preserve them too. For $\Delta^n$, use the spine equivalence of [lem-coef-functor-spine-tower-mapping-descent]. Build the spine by successively adjoining its n edges along their shared vertices. At each adjoining, [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-excision] gives a homotopy pullback of mapping spaces. Its terms preserve I-colimits by the arrow case and induction, and the same finite-limit comparison completes the induction. For n=0 this is precisely compactness of the single vertex. Thus all simplex-shaped pointwise compact diagrams are compact.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.4.13, proof (1)-(3), and Lemma 5.3.4.9 (online, not archived)

proof.text: Extend Step 2 by induction on dimension to every $\kappa$-small finite-dimensional simplicial set L. For dimension zero, its functor category is a product over its fewer than $\kappa$ vertices; its mapping space is the corresponding product, directly from the internal-functor definition. Such products preserve I-colimits by [lem-coef-spaces-kappa-limit-filtered-colimit]. At dimension n, attach the coproduct of the nondegenerate n-simplices to the (n-1)-skeleton along their boundary coproduct. The boundary diagrams are compact by induction, the simplex diagrams by Step 2, and the coproducts of mapping spaces are products of fewer than $\kappa$ spaces. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-excision] to this pushout and [lem-coef-spaces-kappa-limit-filtered-colimit] to its products and homotopy pullback. This proves compactness at dimension n. Here the attaching square is a degreewise pushout: by [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-set-nondegenerate-decomposition], every simplex outside the (n-1)-skeleton is uniquely a degeneracy of one of the attached nondegenerate n-simplices. Distinct such cells meet only in the skeleton, and their boundary maps land there. This proves the stated pushout without requiring a finiteness assumption on the set of cells. Finally $K=\bigcup_n\operatorname{sk}_nK$. The tower formula of [lem-coef-functor-spine-tower-mapping-descent] expresses its mapping space as the limit of the mapping spaces on these skeleta. Since $\kappa$ is uncountable, $N(\mathbb N^{\mathrm{op}})$ is $\kappa$-small. Its limit commutes with I-colimits by [lem-coef-spaces-kappa-limit-filtered-colimit]. Naturality of the mapping formulas and pointwise colimits in Step 1 identify the resulting comparison with the compactness comparison for K. This proves the last clause of the item, including the empty shape (whose mapping space is terminal).

Let $D\subseteq\mathcal C$ be the replete full subcategory of all $\kappa$-compact objects. By [lem-coef-accessible-compact-slice-density], D is essentially small and every $D_{/x}$ is essentially small and $\kappa$-filtered, with its canonical source diagram having colimit x. The category $\mathcal C$ admits every small $\lambda$-filtered colimit by its $\lambda$-accessibility [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category]. Hence for every $\kappa$-small $\lambda$-filtered shape J, the colimit in $\mathcal C$ of a J-diagram in D exists. It remains $\kappa$-compact by [lem-coef-compact-small-colimits], so lies in D. The slice-colimit clause of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-slice-sections] now proves that $D_{/x}$ admits these colimits, computed on sources, and that postcomposition along every $x\to y$ preserves them. This verifies separately the smaller-filtered-colimit hypotheses that the section theorem needs; $\kappa$-accessibility alone would not supply them.

source.place: Proposition 5.4.4.3, fiber hypotheses for Lemma 5.4.4.2; Corollary 5.3.4.15 (online, not archived)

proof.text: Fix $p:K\to\mathcal C$ and apply [lem-coef-infinity-relative-slice-sections] to D and p. Its fibration $E_D\to K$ has fibers $D_{/p(v)}$, with transports given by postcomposition. Step 4 gives $\kappa$-filtered fibers and all $\kappa$-small $\lambda$-filtered colimits preserved by transport. The hypotheses on $\lambda<\kappa$ and on K are exactly those of [lem-coef-filtered-cocartesian-section-cofinality]. Therefore the category B of all sections is $\kappa$-filtered, and every evaluation $B\to D_{/p(v)}$ is cofinal. The relative-slice statement identifies B with pairs $(d,\alpha:d\to p)$ and says it is essentially small. In particular it includes the full coherent transformations; no truncation to the homotopy category or to sets of arrows is made.

source.place: Proposition 5.4.4.3, relative-slice construction and application of Lemma 5.4.4.2 (online, not archived)

proof.text: Choose a small quasicategory $B_0$ and a functor equivalence $e:B_0\to B$; it exists because B is essentially small [lem-coef-infinity-relative-slice-sections]. Projecting a pair $(d,\alpha)$ to d and composing with e gives $r:B_0\to\mathcal F$ and a coherent cocone $r\to p$. For each vertex v its evaluation is the source diagram on $D_{/p(v)}$ precomposed with $\operatorname{ev}_v\circ e:B_0\to D_{/p(v)}$, with the tautological cocone legs. By Step 5 every comma quasicategory of $\operatorname{ev}_v$ is weakly contractible, so by [lem-coef-infinity-cofinal-colimit-restriction] (with $w$ the identity) every comma quasicategory of $\operatorname{ev}_v\circ e$ is weakly contractible. The quasicategories $B_0$ and $D_{/p(v)}$ fit in the larger universe of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category]; apply [lem-coef-infinity-cofinality-space-test] with that universe as its fixed universe and $\mathcal C$ in a containing one: its condition (3) gives (1), so restriction along $\operatorname{ev}_v\circ e$ carries colimiting cocones in $\mathcal C$ to colimiting cocones. The canonical source cocone has colimit $p(v)$ by [lem-coef-accessible-compact-slice-density]. Thus $r\to p$ is colimiting at every vertex, and hence in $\mathcal F$ by [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits], since $B_0$ is small. If K is empty this last assertion still applies: its functor category is terminal and the pointwise test has no components. Every r-value is a diagram valued in D, hence compact by Steps 2-3.

source.place: Proposition 5.4.4.3, final paragraph: evaluationwise density and cofinality (online, not archived)

proof.text: The small quasicategory $B_0$ is $\kappa$-filtered, being equivalent to the $\kappa$-filtered B of Step 5 (a cocone of a $\kappa$-small diagram in $B_0$ is transported along e and a quasi-inverse). By [lem-coef-infinity-cofinal-kappa-poset] choose a small $\kappa$-filtered poset A and a cofinal functor $u:N(A)\to B_0$. Its cofinality is stated for all cocomplete target quasicategories; in particular, with target the small spaces, it gives condition (2) of [lem-coef-infinity-cofinality-space-test], hence condition (1): restriction along u carries every existing colimiting cocone, in any quasicategory, to a colimiting cocone. Composing with r and restricting the cocone of Step 6 gives the requested $q:N(A)\to\mathcal F$ with colimit p. Each $q(a)$ has values in D. The subcategory $\operatorname{Fun}(K,D)$ is essentially small by [lem-coef-infinity-relative-slice-sections], is full in $\mathcal F$ by the definition of a full subcategory in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and its objects are compact by Steps 2-3. Step 6 says they generate every object by a small $\kappa$-filtered colimit. Together with local smallness and existence of such colimits from Step 1, these are all the clauses of $\kappa$-accessibility in [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category]. This proves the first clause as well as the poset-presentation clause.
